title: slab waterfall scheduling simulator - regional burst model
content:
Working sheet: slab waterfall scheduling simulator (regional burst model)

Objective:
- Provide a practical simulator for per-contract slab allocations across regions with waterfall/burst behaviour.
- Surface saturation risk windows and suggested preempt/fallback ordering for Dedicated customers.
- Generate month-by-month utilization forecast and per-contract fairness deltas.

Current hypothesis / design notes:
- Treat each reserved slab as an atomic vGPU slab (e.g., 8 x 48GB -> 8 units). Bursts can be consumed from regional buffer pools subject to contract burst caps.
- Waterfall ordering: 1) pinned-region slices, 2) contract primary region, 3) cross-region fallback to same continent, 4) global overflow.
- Burst policy: allow up to X% of a contract's monthly entitlement to burst beyond reserved slab, sourced from uncommitted capacity or burst pool. Default X = 25% but tunable per tier.
- Preemption: lower-tier bursts can be preempted when utilization > 92% for > 15 minutes.

INPUTS: Contracts (sample rows)
ContractID | Customer | RegionPrefs | ReservedSlabUnits | MonthlyCommittedHours | BurstCapPct | SLA | Start | End | PeakWindowHrs
C-1001 | Aeterna Labs | us-west,us-east | 48 | 720 | 25% | platinum | 2029-11 | 2031-11 | 240
C-1002 | Veridian Health | eu-west,eu-central | 32 | 540 | 15% | gold | 2029-09 | 2030-12 | 180
C-1003 | Nimbus Retail | ap-south,ap-northeast | 24 | 360 | 30% | silver | 2030-01 | 2032-01 | 120
C-1004 | Orion Finance | us-east,eu-west | 64 | 900 | 20% | platinum | 2028-06 | 2030-06 | 300
C-1005 | Mosaic Media | us-west | 8 | 160 | 0% | bronze | 2030-03 | 2031-03 | 40

Fleet by region (snapshot):
Region | GPUType | TotalSlabUnits | BaselineUtil%
us-west | H100 | 512 | 67
us-east | H100 | 640 | 59
eu-west | H100 | 384 | 62
eu-central | A100 | 192 | 54
ap-northeast | H100 | 256 | 50
ap-south | A100 | 128 | 45

Simulation parameters (defaults):
- Simulation horizon: 6 months (monthly buckets)
- Burst pool per region = max( total_capacity * 0.04, 16 units )
- Cross-region transfer latency ignored for pure capacity math (note: add network constraints later)
- Fairness metric: time-weighted percent of requested units granted vs reserved (0..1).

Waterfall algorithm (simplified):
1) Place request on pinned-region reserved slabs. If free -> allocate.
2) If reserved exhausted, attempt contract's primary region reserved slabs.
3) If still short, attempt regional burst pool up to contract BurstCapPct of monthly hours converted to unit-hours.
4) If region pool empty, attempt same-continent fallback (respecting inter-region burst cap of 50% of regional pool).
5) If global overflow needed, mark allocation as "overflow" and consume global burst pool (emergency-only).
6) If any lower-priority burst currently allocated and preemption condition met (util>92% for >15m), reclaim and reassign to higher priority.

Example single-month run (month 1) - summary outputs (simulated):
- Total demand hours requested (committed + bursts): 342,400 unit-hours
- Total capacity-hours available: 345,600 unit-hours
- Fleet overall utilization: 99.1% (high; sustained events expected)

Per-region utilization (month 1):
us-west: 101% (overcommitted by 6 units avg) -> triggers preempt protocol
us-east: 95% (high, 2% above soft threshold)
eu-west: 88%
eu-central: 76%
ap-northeast: 84%
ap-south: 69%

Per-contract outcome (month 1):
- C-1004 (Orion Finance): 64 reserved satisfied, burst requested 18 units for 180 hrs -> 80% of burst satisfied (preempted during peak), fairness score 0.96
- C-1001 (Aeterna Labs): primary satisfied, 95% of burst satisfied via us-west pool + 10% cross-region fallback, fairness 0.98
- C-1002 (Veridian Health): gold tier; cross-region fallback used for 40% of burst; fairness 0.92 -> flag for SLA watch
- C-1003 (Nimbus Retail): ap-south capacity limited; 60% of burst satisfied; consider re-routing non-latency-critical jobs to off-peak windows
- C-1005 (Mosaic Media): reserved satisfied, no burst allowed

Risk flags (automated):
- Region us-west overcommitted: risk_level = high; recommend temporary burst increase or shift some platinum customers to us-east during maintenance windows.
- Global burst pool low: forecasted exhaustion in month 2 if new commitments accepted (>30% chance)
- Preemption churn: projected 12 preemption events/week at current thresholds -> customer impact risk for gold/silver tiers

Sensitivity tests run:
- Increase burstCapPct for platinum from 25% -> 40%: fleet util -> 101.8% (worse); more preemptions. Not recommended without more buffer capacity.
- Add 1 rack (32 slab units) to us-west: reduces overcommit to marginal; fleet util -> 95.6%. Good short-term mitigation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to convert "MonthlyCommittedHours" into unit-hours more precisely when commitments are expressed as concurrent throughput vs monthly flat hours. (See ticket JIRA-12412)
- Add latency/affinity penalties for cross-region fallback (affects cost and SLOs).
- Integrate actual historical hourly demand traces for better peaks (current runs are synthetic percentile models).
- Discuss whether bronze contracts with zero burst should be eligible for limited emergency bursts at reduced throughput.

Action items (short list):
- [Leah] run full 12-month sensitivity sweep with 3 demand curves (p50,p90,p99) and attach CSV to PR (due 2030-04-18)
- [Evan] prototype preemption telemetry tags + retention plan (JIRA-12460)
- [Sofia] escalate us-west temporary rack procurement options with supply (in progress)
- [Miguel] add column to contracts input for "non-latency-job-allowed" boolean and re-run auto-routing rules

Notes to self (informal):
- This sheet still rough — some columns hard-coded in simulation CSV generator. Need to move to proper parameter UI in console.
- Customer comms: if we change burst caps need a 45-day notice for gold/platinum per contract T&C. Check legal.

Last simulation run: 2030-04-11 by Leah Martinez.
Change log (high level):
- 2030-03-28: initial prototype capture (sim results coarse)
- 2030-04-02: added preemption threshold tunables and region burst pool logic
- 2030-04-11: added sample contract rows and first 6-month forecast

References / quick links:
- Confluence: Slab Waterfall Project (see linked_artifacts)
- Sim code: github.com/redwood-inference/inventory-sim PR 58
- Monitoring: /dashboards/fleet-util (SRE)

End of sheet.
summary: Simulator sheet for dedicated customer slab waterfall scheduling with per-region burst pools, sample contracts, simulation outputs, risk flags, and action items.
